title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 5)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »).

sentences.fr: Fern[an]d a un chat bl[an]c qui s'appelle Flocon.
sentences.en: Fernand has a white cat called Flocon.

sentences.fr: Le chat dort d[an]s la ch[am]bre, près de la l[am]pe.
sentences.en: The cat sleeps in the bedroom, near the lamp.

sentences.fr: Qu[an]d il a faim, il ch[an]te très fort.
sentences.en: When he's hungry, he sings very loudly.

sentences.fr: Fern[an]d lui donne de la vi[an]de.
